steps.text: Place milk, sugar, eggs, oil and vanilla in the blender. Add flour and baking powder. Blend until smooth.
Heat a lightly oiled griddle or frying pan over medium high heat. Pour or scoop the batter onto the griddle, using approximately 1/4 cup for each pancake. Brown on both sides and serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Fast and Easy Pancakes
raw_recipe.description: Quick and easy pancakes that are mixed in your blender! Perfect for those mornings when you have to get breakfast on the table but don't have the time to make anything complicated.
raw_recipe.name: Fast and Easy Pancakes

recipeInstructions.text: Place milk, sugar, eggs, oil and vanilla in the blender. Add flour and baking powder. Blend until smooth.
Heat a lightly oiled griddle or frying pan over medium high heat. Pour or scoop the batter onto the griddle, using approximately 1/4 cup for each pancake. Brown on both sides and serve hot.

review.reviewBody: Delicious! I changed the sugar to 1/2 cup and used a whisk to mix the batter instead of a blender. They were very fluffy! The reviewers that had flat pancakes likely mixed the batter too much. You want the batter to be a little lumpy.

Excellent fast recipe if you are short on time. I also changed the sugar to 1/2 cup, it was crazy sweet still (but we like that). I think this would have benefitted from about a 1/4 teaspoon of salt, it was missing some kind of dimension and I think that was it. I used a hand mixer to combine instead of a blender and finished mixing with a spatula. I whipped my eggs first before adding them to the rest of the wet ingredients and I had no problems with flat or dense pancakes.

OK Here are some more hints. 1. make sure your baking powder is fresh and double acting. 2. make sure you don't over mix.. if you do it will make gluten and that is what will make it tough and chewy. it's better to mix in a bowl with a whisk than in the blender. 3. add a pinch of salt, it make everything else taste better. 4. mix all dry together, then mix in the wet, then the baking powder wont react until you want it to. 5. have whatever your cooking on hot and ready before you mix the wet, that way you can cook before all the baking powder is used up. 6. add fun mix-ins like fruit, nuts, or chocolate. lastly have fun and don't be so critical. mistakes are how you learn. if you don't like how it turned out this time, tweak it and try again. that's what makes cooking so great! thanks for the recipe. I used apple sauce instead of the oil, and added almond extract for that extra kick. thanks again

I made it with sweetened vanilla almond milk due to our lactose sensitivities. I still added the vanilla. They were wonderful! They made plenty for the 3 of us, with more left over for tomorrow. I also didn't make it in my blender (blender issues). They can be made by hand; however, I would recommend mixing them differently if you're going to do it that way.

FYI These will spread out on the cooking surface. They aren't thick. They are good though!

I'm giving this 4 stars because they are fast and easy, and my husband was happy with them. But they are not pancakes, they are modified crepes, hence the "rubbery" texture. They are MUCH too sweet to me, so the second time I made them I reduced the sugar to 1/3 cup, perfect amount of sweetness for me. I also found the vanilla flavor overwhelming so I reduced it to 1/2 teaspoon, which was fine. This recipe also has a TON of baking powder in it, which is funny because it doesn't do much for the pancakes, they are almost completely flat. The second time I made them I even let the batter sit for 15-20 minutes, hoping that it would activate enough to make a difference, it didn't. Maybe just one egg would make the batter lighter. I think I'll tweak this a bit then update the review and let you all know how it goes.

I cut way back on the sugar, because that seemed like too much to me. As a result, I had to add more flour because the batter was too runny. The batter still was pretty thin, but the pancakes puffed up very nicely and were good. Everyone's taste is different, and I think I would enjoy these even more with no sugar. I might try subbing some whole wheat flour too. It's a good base recipe that you can modify to your family's tastes.

I wanted to make some pancakes and had no batter mix. With a group of 7 hungry people to feed breakfast... I read the ingredients and reviews and decided to try it out following some suggestions in another review of using 1/2 cup of sugar and I blended it using a hand mixer. A decent amount of pancakes came out and they were sooo good! I will repeat this recipe and is on my favorites list. Thank you!

Perfect! I used my immersion blender with the whisk attachment. Halved the recipe, doubled the vanilla, omitted the oil and made them in a well buttered skillet. YUM! :D Done in less than 10 minutes from start to finish (including washing my dishes by hand!).
Great texture and cooked up great, but way too sweet. Some people say change the sugar to 1/2 but I only use 1/4 cup because I don't like sweet pancakes.
Love the blender method. Too sweet for us, cut sugar back to 1/4 cup and they are perfect!

My kids (2 and 4) loved this recipe. I didn't have any vanilla, so I subbed almond extract. I also used an applesauce/baking powder mixture instead of eggs. I love this recipe because it doesn't taste like flour like a lot of other recipes I've tried and the pancakes turn out fluffy and light.
It tasted delicious
This is candy disguised as pancakes. If I could give this a zero stars, I would have.
I am a student but i made this on my own. This pancake is really good really sweet so if you do not like sweet i do not recommend this for you. i love the texture really good for kids,and families.
Perfect, will make again!
I substituted milk 4 Silk Almond milk & oil 4 Olive Oil
Good and easy I also added vanilla
Did not make any changes and will NOT make it again.
It was amazing!!!!!!

Super Easy, Fast and Delicious! Blend the ingredients, pour on oiled or buttered griddle - that’s it. Clean up is a breeze. We like our pancakes on the sweet side so the sugar amount was perfect for us. I also like to sprinkle on my favorite granola right before I flip them.
